keyIdea:
**Metric:** $10\text{ mm} = 1\text{ cm}$, $100\text{ cm} = 1\text{ m}$, $1000\text{ m} = 1\text{ km}$, $1000\text{ g} = 1\text{ kg}$, $1000\text{ kg} = 1$ tonne, $1000\text{ ml} = 1$ litre, $1\text{ cm}^3 = 1\text{ ml}$.

Big unit to small unit: multiply; small to big: divide.

**Area and volume:** square or cube the length factor. Since $1\text{ m} = 100\text{ cm}$,
$$1\text{ m}^2 = 100^2\text{ cm}^2 = 10\,000\text{ cm}^2, \qquad 1\text{ m}^3 = 100^3\text{ cm}^3 = 1\,000\,000\text{ cm}^3$$

**Customary units (US):** $12$ in $= 1$ ft, $3$ ft $= 1$ yd, $5280$ ft $= 1$ mi, $16$ oz $= 1$ lb. These are not base 10. Useful links: $1$ in $= 2.54$ cm, $1$ kg $\approx 2.2$ lb, $5$ miles $\approx 8$ km.

**Time:** $60$ s $= 1$ min, $60$ min $= 1$ h, so decimal hours are not minutes: $0.4\text{ h} = 0.4 \times 60 = 24$ min.

**Rates (dimensional analysis):** multiply by conversion factors written as fractions equal to 1 so the unwanted units cancel, e.g. $72\text{ km/h} = 72 \times \dfrac{1000\text{ m}}{1\text{ km}} \times \dfrac{1\text{ h}}{3600\text{ s}} = 20\text{ m/s}$. Choose a unit that suits the size of the quantity, and round to an accuracy that matches the data.
